title: Botox Cost Per Lead 2026: Click Prices and Budgets
summary: A click on 'botox near me' averages $14.40 in the US. See Botox cost per lead at 5%, 10% and 15% conversion, Google vs Meta, and a monthly ad budget.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- A click on the main Botox searches costs $10.26 to $14.40 on average in the US: $11.27 for 'botox', $14.40 for 'botox near me' and $10.26 for 'botox injections'.
- At a 10% click-to-lead conversion rate, a $11.27 click works out to about $113 per lead ($11.27 / 0.10 = $112.70). At 5% it is $225 and at 15% it is $75.
- LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks for beauty and personal care show $39.25 per lead on Google search and $50.91 on Meta lead campaigns, so Meta ran about 30% higher in that category.
- A sensible starting budget is: new patients you want, divided by your booking rate, times your cost per lead.


## What a click costs


Botox is one of the most searched cosmetic treatments in the US, and the clicks are priced to match. These are the three main searches and what a click costs at the top of Google in the US.


Keyword US searches a month Average cost per click Top-of-page range


botox 165,000 $11.27 $3.43 to $12.39


botox near me 165,000 $14.40 $3.92 to $23.24


botox injections 9,900 $10.26 $2.79 to $10.90


The spread inside each range comes from three things. Urgency matters: 'near me' searches come from people ready to book, so more advertisers bid hard on them. Competition matters: med spas, dermatology offices and other injectors in your area all bid on the same words. City matters too, because the same search costs more where more clinics compete for it. That is why the top end of 'botox near me' reaches $23.24 while the low end sits at $3.92.


## From click to cost per lead


You do not pay for leads on Google Search. You pay for clicks, and a share of those clicks turn into a call, a form or a booking request. Divide the click price by that share and you get your cost per lead. The table uses the average click on 'botox', $11.27.


Click-to-lead conversion rate Cost per lead ($11.27 / rate) Cost per booked patient (example: 1 in 3 leads books)


5% $225 $676


10% $113 $338


15% $75 $225


The booking rate in the last column is an example input, not a benchmark. Swap in your own number. A fast reply and a clear booking page move both columns more than a small change in bids does. To run your own figures, use the[cost per lead calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cost-per-lead-calculator) .


## Google Ads vs Local Services Ads vs Facebook for Botox injectors


Google Ads (Search) Local Services Ads Facebook and Instagram (Meta)


How you pay Per click Per lead, with the price set by Google by category and area For ad delivery, with lead campaigns measured by cost per lead


Intent High. The person typed 'botox near me' High, but only where your category is offered Lower. The person was scrolling, not searching


When it wins for Botox First channel for most injectors, because buyers search by name of the treatment and town Only if your business type is an available category in your area. Botox injecting is not one to plan around, so check before you count on it Offers, new patient promotions, and reminders to people who have not booked yet


On Local Services Ads, Google decides the lead price by category and area, so there is no single figure to quote. Read the[guide to Google Local Services Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) to see how the program works and how to check eligibility.


For benchmark cost per lead, LocaliQ's 2026 figures for beauty and personal care are $39.25 on Google search and $50.91 on Meta lead campaigns. The difference is $11.66, so Meta cost about 30% more per lead ($50.91 / $39.25 = 1.30). LocaliQ's all-industry figures go the other way: $66.69 for Google search and $27.39 for Meta lead campaigns. That is a reason not to assume one channel is always cheaper. These benchmarks cover whole categories, not Botox injectors, and the average Botox click price is high enough that your own number may land above them. See[average cost per lead by industry](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry) for more comparisons.


## How much to spend each month


Use this formula:


**Monthly budget = (new patients you want / booking rate) x cost per lead**


Here is a worked example with stated inputs:


1. You want 10 new Botox patients a month.
2. Say 1 in 3 leads books (an example, use your own rate). You need 10 x 3 = 30 leads.
3. At $113 per lead (a 10% conversion rate on a $11.27 click), the budget is 30 x $113 = $3,390 a month.
4. At LocaliQ's 2026 beauty and personal care Google search figure of $39.25, the same 30 leads would cost 30 x $39.25 = $1,177.50. Your real number will fall somewhere between, and a month or two of data will show where.


Start on one channel, usually Google Search, until your cost per lead is steady. Then add Meta as a second channel rather than splitting a small budget across both. For setup details, read the[Botox advertising guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/botox-advertising) .


## How to lower your cost per lead


- **Make one clear first-visit offer.** A consultation or a new patient offer gives a visitor a reason to act now. Test one offer at a time so you know which one works. See what Botox injectors run on Facebook in the[Botox ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/botox-ads) .
- **Send clicks to a dedicated landing page.** Show your injector credentials, reviews, the treatment areas you cover and a single booking button. A homepage with ten menu options loses visitors.
- **Answer fast.** Answer calls, or text back missed ones, within minutes. A lead who called three clinics will often book with the first one that replies.
- **Add negative keywords.** Block searches like 'botox training', 'botox certification', 'botox jobs' and 'botox for sale', which bring clicks from people who will never book a visit.
- **Limit your service area.** Target the towns around your clinic instead of a wide region. Because 'botox near me' has a top-of-page range of $3.92 to $23.24, set a maximum bid so you do not pay the top of that range on every click.
- **Keep the lead form short.** Ask for name, phone, treatment area and preferred day. Each extra field cuts submissions, but one qualifying question keeps out leads that were never going to book.
